100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 29, 1926, the League of Nations convened in Geneva to address escalating tensions in Europe, particularly concerning disarmament and potential conflicts. In the United States, the Senate continued debates over the controversial Kellogg-Briand Pact, aimed at renouncing war as a means of national policy. Meanwhile, in Berlin, the German government faced political turmoil as the economic crisis deepened, leading to protests and calls for reform.
